answer: A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The comet multiplier is published, charged in horizon, and falcon lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 7 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 3332 identities would post 4982 proofs and burn roughly 15 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
